unit.why: A memorate told by the author's father-in-law: the tsaddik of Rozdol wrote his books wrapped in tallit and tefillin and, on his deathbed, looked over his manuscripts and spoke about them.

stories.start_quote: סיפר לי חותני הרה״צ המפו' מו"ה מנחם מענדל
stories.summary_en: The tsaddik of Rozdol wrote his books every day in seclusion, wrapped in tallit and tefillin; before his death he asked for his writings and declared that, having no son, he relied on his book, which seemed written by an angel and which he himself now had to strain to understand.

tags.why: He wrote his books while wearing tallit and tefillin.
He wrote shut away from others.
He devoted daily work to composing Torah books.

quotes: ובעת שחלה חוליו האחרון ביקש לפני פטירתו
שיגישו לידו הכתבים שלו ועיין בהם
tags.why: The deathbed scene and his last words form the climax.

quotes: ובעת שחלה חוליו האחרון ביקש לפני פטירתו
tags.why: His final illness and death are depicted.

quotes: בן הצדיקת מרת הינדא ע"ה בתו
מיר לאזין נישט איבער קיין בן זכר
tags.why: The tsaddik's grandson tells the story; his daughter is named and his lack of a son is discussed.

quotes: בן הצדיקת מרת הינדא ע"ה בתו
tags.why: His daughter Hinda is named but does not act.
The story is framed as told by a named tsaddik, the author's father-in-law.
The story's point is the holiness with which he composed his writings.
He was wrapped in a tallit as a sign of holiness while writing.
